reviews.feedback: internal/store/customers.go ImportCustomers (email_taken check, ~line 74-76): the lookup uses the global customersByEmail map, which keeps only one customer per email across all organizations. If Acme creates x@example.com, then Globex creates the same address via CreateCustomer (allowed; the map is overwritten to Globex's customer), an import into Acme of x@example.com finds Globex's customer, fails the OrgID check, and does not return email_taken. The row is then created, so Acme ends up with two customers sharing an email, which the spec forbids. Fix: check the importing organization's own customers instead of the global map, e.g. build the set of normalized emails of s.customers where OrgID == orgID under s.mu, and use it for email_taken. Add a test for the reverse order (Acme creates, Globex creates the same email, Acme imports it expecting 422 email_taken on that row). The CreateCustomer map overwrite is pre-existing and outside this task.
